subject: Embeddings migration & integration follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Embeddings migration & integration follow-up

Alex — really appreciated your time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side after the discovery: 

Call recap (high level)
- Goal: migrate from ProviderX to Redwood for semantic search + reranking across your product docs and support KB.
- Primary constraints: preserve IDs/metadata, minimize downtime for search, cost target ~30% lower per-query, keep latency SLOs (~<50ms median for top-k).

Integration / architecture notes
- SDK setup: recommend starting with Redwood JS SDK v1.4 (linked in attached sdk-setup.md). Example upsert + query flows are in the guide.
- Auth: for Hosted API use API keys scoped to embeddings/upsert. For Dedicated/Private we recommend short-lived tokens + KMS-managed keys for key rotation.
- Routing: route user-facing queries to the dedicated embeddings index + low-latency ANN store; fallback routing policy to cheaper model for non-critical queries to keep costs down.
- Structured output / tool-calling: if you plan to use LLMs to generate metadata during ingestion, use function-calling to enforce schema (we can share templates).

Embeddings-specific recommendations
- Vector dimensions: Redwood supports common dims (e.g., 768, 1024, 1536). For highest semantic fidelity on Acme content we recommend 1536 where feasible.
- Batching / upsert sizing: recommended upsert batch size is 128–512 vectors for reliability; you can push up to ~1k per call depending on vector size and memory limits on your index node.
- Normalization: we recommend L2-normalizing vectors and using cosine similarity as the ANN distance metric for best cross-model compatibility.
- Rerankers: keep a lightweight cross-encoder reranker for top-50 candidates to maintain precision after migration.

Migration checklist (short)
1) Export embeddings & metadata from ProviderX (we can provide scripts).
2) Validate sample re-embeds (run 10k docs through Redwood embedding model and compare retrieval A/B).
3) Full batch re-embed + upsert to Redwood index (use batching, monitor memory).
4) Run A/B traffic (10–20%) with reranker on results, validate metrics.
5) Flip traffic and decommission ProviderX.

Attachments include a proposed migration plan, SDK quickstart, and a sample batch CSV. Estimated timeline: 2–4 weeks from kickoff for a typical mid-sized KB (50–200k docs), assuming we get your sample dataset.

Next steps
- Could you share a ~5–10k sample export (ids + text + metadata) so we can run a pilot?
- Proposed times for technical deep-dive: Thu 2026-07-23 09:00–10:00 PT or Fri 2026-07-24 11:00–12:00 PT.

Thanks — looping in Nikhil (solutions) and Dylan (engineering) to schedule the deep-dive and confirm the migration playbook.

—
Marissa Cole

Thanks Alex — answers inline below and a couple of logistics items.

> Dimension compatibility: we currently have 1024-dim vectors from ProviderX. If we re-embed to 1536 will that break any of our existing pipelines (ids/metadata)? Do you support hybrid indexes with mixed dims?
- Short answer: metadata and IDs are orthogonal to vector dimension. You can preserve your IDs/fields. Hybrid indexes with mixed dims are not recommended for production (distance metrics differ); for best results we re-embed to a single target dim (we recommend 1536). If you need to compare old vs new we suggest keeping an archival index of ProviderX vectors and running A/B retrieval.

> Bulk upsert: you mentioned up to ~1k per call — what do you recommend for an initial full reindex of ~120k docs to avoid timeouts?
- Recommendation: do segmented upserts of 250–500 vectors per request with concurrency of 4–8 workers. That provides stable throughput without spiking index memory. Example: 120k docs -> 500 per batch -> ~240 calls per worker; with 4 workers that finishes in a few hours depending on network. We include retries and backoff in our sample script (sdk-setup.md).

> IDs & metadata: can we preserve our original doc IDs and custom metadata fields (tags, product ids)?
- Yes — our upsert API accepts client-side IDs and arbitrary metadata fields. We recommend validating a small sample to confirm mapping.

> Compliance: our security team will need SOC 2 evidence and a simple data flow diagram for the pilot.
- We have SOC 2 Type II documentation and a pilot data flow diagram — shared in the docs link (see related_links). I can also provide a short one-page diagram specific to the pilot if you send the architecture constraints.

Logistics
- Deep-dive: confirmed Thu 2026-07-23 09:00 PT. I'll send a calendar invite and include a short agenda (pilot scope, sample dataset, migration script walk-through, rollback plan).
- Please upload the 5–10k sample export to the shared Drive link or reply with s3 details; we'll run the sample re-embed and share retrieval stats.

I'll follow up after the deep-dive with an updated migration plan and timeline.
